question: On the Georgia Broker national exam content outline, which content area carries the single LARGEST weight?
choice_a: Contracts, at 19% of the national exam
choice_b: Agency, at 13% of the national exam
choice_c: Practice of Real Estate, at 12% of the national exam
choice_d: Financing, at 9% of the national exam
explanation: Per the GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin's national content outline, Contracts is weighted 19% for the broker exam -- the single largest category, ahead of Practice of Real Estate (12%) and Agency (13%).
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, national exam content outline

question: On the Georgia Broker national exam content outline, how are Real Estate Calculations weighted compared to Land Use Controls?
choice_a: Real Estate Calculations is weighted 15%, three times Land Use Controls
choice_b: Real Estate Calculations is weighted 6%, slightly more than Land Use Controls at 5%
choice_d: Land Use Controls outweighs Real Estate Calculations, 9% to 6%
explanation: The national content outline weights Real Estate Calculations at 6% and Land Use Controls at 5% -- both are comparatively minor categories relative to Contracts (19%) or Agency (13%).
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, national exam content outline

question: The national exam content outline's 'Practice of Real Estate' category (12%) includes a sub-section that applies only to the broker exam and not the salesperson exam. What is that sub-section?
explanation: The Practice of Real Estate category's content outline includes a 'Supervisory Responsibilities' sub-item flagged as 'BROKER ONLY,' reflecting the additional supervisory content tested on the broker national exam that does not appear on the salesperson exam.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, national exam content outline

question: The national outline's Property Management category (5%) includes several sub-items marked 'BROKER ONLY.' What do those sub-items generally cover?
choice_d: Trust funds, contracts, and risk management specific to property management
explanation: Within the 5%-weighted Property Management category, several sub-items on trust funds, contracts, and risk management are flagged 'BROKER ONLY,' reflecting broker-level property-management responsibilities not tested on the salesperson exam.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, national exam content outline

question: Unlike the conventional single-best-answer format used elsewhere on the exam, what distinctive item format does the Georgia Broker National exam's bulletin sample include?
choice_a: Scenario-based items using multi-option, weighted scoring
choice_b: True/false items only, with no multiple-choice items
choice_c: Fill-in-the-blank numeric entry with no answer choices provided
choice_d: Oral-response items scored by a live proctor
explanation: The GREC/PSI bulletin's own sample materials show the Broker National exam using scenario-based items with multi-option, weighted scoring, in addition to conventional items -- a more complex evaluation format than a simple single-correct-answer multiple-choice item.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, sample exam item format

question: Before the timed portion of the Georgia broker exam begins, what does the PSI test center provide?
choice_b: An untimed tutorial of up to 15 minutes
choice_c: No tutorial of any kind -- the timed exam begins the instant the candidate is seated
explanation: Per the GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, candidates are given an untimed tutorial of up to 15 minutes before the timed examination begins, to familiarize them with the testing software and interface.

question: How far in advance of their scheduled appointment time does the GREC/PSI bulletin instruct broker candidates to arrive at the test center?
choice_d: The bulletin does not specify any arrival-time instruction
explanation: The current GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin instructs candidates to arrive 30 minutes before their scheduled appointment time, to allow time for check-in procedures.

question: Does Georgia's licensing scheme provide any exemption from the broker prelicense education or exam requirement for applicants who are already licensed attorneys?
choice_a: Yes -- any active member of the State Bar of Georgia is automatically issued a broker license without examination
choice_b: Yes -- attorneys are exempt from the exam only, but must still complete all coursework
choice_c: Yes -- attorneys need only complete 15 hours of coursework instead of 60
choice_d: No -- no attorney-in-lieu-of-education-or-experience exemption is found anywhere in GAC 520-1-.04, GAC 520-2, or the current GREC/PSI bulletin; a licensed attorney must still satisfy the standard broker prerequisites
explanation: No attorney-in-lieu-of-experience-or-education exemption exists in Georgia's real estate broker licensing scheme; this is a confirmed absence, not merely an unresearched gap, after review of the governing rules and the current candidate bulletin. Licensed attorneys applying for a Georgia broker license must satisfy the same prelicense education, experience, and exam requirements as any other applicant.
source_note: Confirmed absence in Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.04, 520-2; GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin

question: How is Georgia's separate 48-item Community Association Manager (CAM) exam broken down between its two content areas?
choice_a: 14 items on Laws and Rules, 34 items on Practice
choice_b: 24 items on Laws and Rules, 24 items on Practice
choice_c: 34 items on Laws and Rules, 14 items on Practice
choice_d: 48 items entirely on Practice, with no separate Laws and Rules section
explanation: Georgia's separate 48-item CAM exam is broken down as 14 items on Laws/Rules and 34 items on Practice -- a distinct structure from the 48-item Georgia Broker Supplement Examination (31 State Laws and Rules / 12 Management / 5 Closing and Calculations).
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, CAM exam content outline

question: A salesperson wants to know whether their existing 75-hour Salesperson Prelicense Course automatically counts toward the separate broker education prerequisite. What is the accurate answer?
choice_a: Yes -- completing the 75-hour salesperson course is itself sufficient to satisfy the broker education prerequisite with no further coursework
choice_b: The 75-hour salesperson course, by itself, does NOT satisfy the broker education prerequisite -- broker education requires one of the distinct routes (60-hour Broker's Prelicense Course, qualifying college coursework, or another jurisdiction's approved 60-hour prelicense coursework)
choice_c: Yes, but only if the salesperson has been licensed for at least 10 years
choice_d: No coursework of any kind is required for the broker exam once a candidate already holds an active salesperson license
explanation: The 75-hour Salesperson Prelicense Course satisfies salesperson-level education requirements, but does not by itself satisfy the separate broker education prerequisite, which requires one of its own distinct routes: the 60-hour Broker's Prelicense Course, qualifying college/law-school coursework, or another jurisdiction's approved 60-hour prelicense coursework.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, broker education requirements

question: An applicant's certified GCIC criminal history report is dated 75 days before the date the broker application is submitted to GREC. Does this report satisfy the application requirement?
choice_a: Yes -- any report dated within the current calendar year is acceptable
choice_b: Yes -- the 60-day rule applies only to salesperson applicants, not broker applicants
choice_c: No -- the report must be no more than 60 days old, so a 75-day-old report does not satisfy the requirement
choice_d: Yes -- there is no maximum age for the GCIC report as long as it shows no disqualifying convictions
explanation: Applicants must submit a certified GCIC criminal history report (or equivalent from their state of residency) that is no more than 60 days old at the time of application; a 75-day-old report would need to be replaced with a current one before the application could be accepted.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, background check requirement

question: An applicant for an Associate Broker position passes the exam and affiliates immediately with a sponsoring firm. Roughly how soon can that applicant begin actively practicing under an Active license?
choice_a: Only after a mandatory 30-day waiting period following the exam
choice_b: Only after GREC's board meets in person to approve the individual application, which can take several months
choice_c: Only after completing an additional 25-hour post-licensing course first
choice_d: Immediately -- the Active license is issued directly at the PSI test center upon passing, provided a signed Sponsoring Broker Statement naming the firm is submitted
explanation: An applicant who affiliates with a sponsoring firm and submits a signed Sponsoring Broker Statement can receive an Active license directly at the PSI test center upon passing the exam, allowing the applicant to begin practicing as an Associate Broker essentially immediately, without a separate waiting period or in-person board approval.
source_note: GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, license issuance at test center

question: A broker's license expired because the licensee did not timely complete their continuing education for a renewal cycle. What CE obligation applies once the license is reinstated?
choice_a: The standard renewal-cycle CE requirement of 36 instructional hours per 4-year period, with at least 3 hours on license-law topics, continues to apply -- Georgia's rules do not create a separate, reduced CE track for licenses lapsed for CE noncompliance
choice_b: No further CE is ever required once a license has lapsed and been reinstated
choice_c: The CE requirement doubles permanently to 72 hours per cycle as a penalty for the lapse
choice_d: CE requirements are waived permanently for any licensee who has ever let a license lapse
explanation: Georgia's standard CE renewal requirement -- 36 instructional hours per 4-year cycle, at least 3 of which must be on license-law topics under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.05 -- continues to apply on an ongoing basis; the rule does not establish a separate reduced-CE track tied to a prior lapse.

question: Georgia's broker felony/moral-turpitude ineligibility bar runs 10 years 'from the later of conviction, sentencing, or release from incarceration.' What does the phrase 'the later of' mean in applying this rule?
choice_a: The 10-year clock starts from whichever of those three events occurred FIRST
choice_b: The 10-year clock starts from whichever of those three events occurred MOST RECENTLY (i.e., last in time), not from the earliest of the three
choice_c: All three events must occur simultaneously for the bar to apply at all
choice_d: The applicant may choose which of the three dates to use, whichever is most favorable to them
explanation: 'The later of' conviction, sentencing, or release from incarceration means the 10-year enhanced ineligibility period for Broker/Associate Broker applicants begins running from whichever of those three events happened most recently -- typically release from incarceration, if incarceration followed sentencing.

question: Besides the Lawful Presence Affidavit's age attestation, what is the substantive purpose of that affidavit within a Georgia broker application?
choice_a: It certifies the applicant has never been convicted of a felony
choice_b: It certifies the applicant has completed all required prelicense coursework
choice_c: It is a notarized statement in which the applicant verifies their lawful presence in the United States, required as part of every Georgia occupational license application under state law
choice_d: It is used exclusively to verify the applicant's Georgia residency address
explanation: The Lawful Presence Affidavit is a notarized statement, required with every Georgia occupational license application (including real estate broker applications) under state law, in which the applicant verifies their lawful presence in the United States -- distinct in purpose from the criminal-history report or the education-completion documentation submitted separately.
